PanoRef coverage optimizer review and follow-up work.

Current state:
- Latest head implements the coverage-engine algorithm (17 files, worker, UI, tests). Joint mode is genuinely joint (evaluates candidate pairs, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality/contribution tie-breakers). Fixed-first and joint branches share a coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine, local offsets).
- Surface sampler is deterministic and area-weighted via barycentric coordinates. Origin evaluation includes segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values.
- Tests added: deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, both search modes.
- Recent patch aligned runtime shader with optimizer intent: replaced old distance-only blend heuristic with angle/texel-quality selection and winner-takes-most weighting (pow(score,4)), plus dominant-mode bias (1.15 for blend modes 2/3). Removed stale test guarding old constant; multiOriginInteraction.test.ts now 36 tests passing.

Review verdict (from user review):
- Algorithm architecture for normal graybox sets: 8/10
- Correctness of two search modes: 7.5/10
- Readiness for complex imported sets: 4/10
- Overall: promising, not production-ready yet.

Blockers identified:
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates. Candidate clearance uses per-object AABB distance with 0.3m rejection; a point inside an AABB gets zero clearance. A single imported SceneObject enclosing a room can reject all sensible origins. Fix: use actual geometry clearance (point-to-triangle distance / sphere intersection / shapecast), or at least per connected mesh / spatial cluster bounds, not per imported set object. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor/walls/empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded to JS objects with independent Vec3 arrays, normals, IDs, area; structured-cloned into worker. For 3M triangles, minimum packed data ~144MB, actual much larger. BVH sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays → GC pressure. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals?, meshRanges, transforms), transfer ArrayBuffers, use three-mesh-bvh or flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, avoid expanding indexed vertices per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before worker post, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning all block UI. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk/yield between meshes.
4. “Apply to selected panorama pair” is conceptually wrong. Workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references (updatePanoReference(..., {origin})). Changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and origin; for fixed-first move next capture origin to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; for joint, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both with actual origins. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both, used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound. Also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. “Four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. Offsets generated around original seed at spacing/2, /4, /8, /16; system does not select best half-step result and re-center quarter-step search around new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sampling, but not the planned coordinate/pattern refinement loop.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height. Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; runtime shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible. Optimizer may prefer frontal-angle source while renderer favors closer but more grazing source. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Partially addressed by recent patch, but still a known mismatch to close fully.)

Testing gaps:
- No test for one large imported object containing an entire room.
- No 100k+ triangle performance fixture (only BVH-construction test, not full optimizer integration test).
- No reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant test.
- No fixed-first candidate separation test.
- No sloped/multilevel floor test.
- No existing panorama origins immutability test.
- No candidate generation inside concave imported geometry test.
- No GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so reported test suite not independently enforced in CI.

Latest verification results:
- unit: npm test -- --run → 42 test files, 371 tests passed; notable long tests: projectionCoverage.test.ts 10 tests ~39.2s (“runs both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture”), occlusion/projected compile/receive tests pass with real WebGL readback.
- lint: tsc --noEmit passed.
- build: vite build passed.

User directive (turn 762):
- Rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict.
- Add an allowed-floor-region mechanism—or at least robust imported-floor component filtering.
- Run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test.
- Goal: accomplish the above, then spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is fully complete; have it report what is still lacking; fix that; repeat until subagent cannot find holes.

Open continuation constraints:
- Must rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict before further work.
- Must add allowed-floor-region / imported-floor component filtering.
- Must run a real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not just BVH construction).
- Must then run adversarial subagent verification loop until no holes found.
- The 7 blockers above remain the concrete correctness/scaling/workflow gap list to drive implementation and verification.

Changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and origin; for fixed-first move next capture origin to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; for joint, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both with actual origins. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both, used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound. Also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. “Four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. Offsets generated around original seed at spacing/2, /4, /8, /16; system does not select best half-step result and re-center quarter-step search around new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sampling, but not the planned coordinate/pattern refinement loop.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height. Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; runtime shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible. Optimizer may prefer frontal-angle source while renderer favors closer but more grazing source. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Partially addressed by recent patch, but still a known mismatch to close fully.)

A single imported SceneObject enclosing a room can reject all sensible origins. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor/walls/empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded to JS objects with independent Vec3 arrays, normals, IDs, area; structured-cloned into worker. For 3M triangles, minimum packed data ~144MB, actual much larger. BVH sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays → GC pressure. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals?, meshRanges, transforms), transfer ArrayBuffers, use three-mesh-bvh or flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, avoid expanding indexed vertices per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before worker post, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning all block UI. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk/yield between meshes.
4. “Apply to selected panorama pair” is conceptually wrong. Workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references (updatePanoReference(..., {origin})). Changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and origin; for fixed-first move next capture origin to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; for joint, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both with actual origins. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both, used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound. Also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. “Four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. Offsets generated around original seed at spacing/2, /4, /8, /16; system does not select best half-step result and re-center quarter-step search around new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sampling, but not the planned coordinate/pattern refinement loop.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height. Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; runtime shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor/walls/empty interior.

For 3M triangles, minimum packed data ~144MB, actual much larger. BVH sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays → GC pressure. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals?, meshRanges, transforms), transfer ArrayBuffers, use three-mesh-bvh or flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, avoid expanding indexed vertices per triangle.

Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before worker post, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning all block UI. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk/yield between meshes.

Changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and origin; for fixed-first move next capture origin to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; for joint, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both with actual origins. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both, used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound. Also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. “Four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. Offsets generated around original seed at spacing/2, /4, /8, /16; system does not select best half-step result and re-center quarter-step search around new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sampling, but not the planned coordinate/pattern refinement loop.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height. Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; runtime shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible. Optimizer may prefer frontal-angle source while renderer favors closer but more grazing source. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Partially addressed by recent patch, but still a known mismatch to close fully.)

Blockers identified:
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates. Candidate clearance uses per-object AABB distance with 0.3m rejection; a point inside an AABB gets zero clearance. A single imported SceneObject enclosing a room can reject all sensible origins. Fix: use actual geometry clearance (point-to-triangle distance / sphere intersection / shapecast), or at least per connected mesh / spatial cluster bounds, not per imported set object. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor/walls/empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded to JS objects with independent Vec3 arrays, normals, IDs, area; structured-cloned into worker. For 3M triangles, minimum packed data ~144MB, actual much larger. BVH sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays → GC pressure. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals?, meshRanges, transforms), transfer ArrayBuffers, use three-mesh-bvh or flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, avoid expanding indexed vertices per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before worker post, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning all block UI. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk/yield between meshes.
4. “Apply to selected panorama pair” is conceptually wrong. Workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references (updatePanoReference(..., {origin})). Changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and origin; for fixed-first move next capture origin to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; for joint, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both with actual origins. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both, used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound. Also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. “Four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. Offsets generated around original seed at spacing/2, /4, /8, /16; system does not select best half-step result and re-center quarter-step search around new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sampling, but not the planned coordinate/pattern refinement loop.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height. Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; runtime shader blends only by distance when both panoramas visible. Optimizer may prefer frontal-angle source while renderer favors closer but more grazing source. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Partially addressed by recent patch, but still a known mismatch to close fully.)
